stem: What is the CMDB (Configuration Management Database) schema model?

options.text: A series of connected tables that contain all the assets and business services controlled by a company
A single flat list of purchased hardware
A catalog of approved standard changes

rationale: The CMDB is a set of connected tables modeling the company's assets and business services along with their configurations — the system of record that ITSM processes lean on.

distractor_notes.B: A flat list is exactly what the CMDB improves on; it models connected data, not a single list.
distractor_notes.C: An incident queue is an Incident Management view.
distractor_notes.D: The standard change catalog is a Change Management construct.

stem: How does the CMDB differ from a static asset list?

options.text: It tracks the configuration items and also the relationships between those items
It only stores the purchase price of each asset
It cannot store more than one CI type
It replaces the need for Change Management

rationale: The CMDB's value is in the connections: it records CIs and the relationships between them, so you can see how a database supports an application that supports a business service.

distractor_notes.B: The CMDB stores far more than price; relationships are its key advantage.
distractor_notes.C: The CMDB models many CI types across its class hierarchy.
distractor_notes.D: The CMDB informs Change Management; it doesn't replace it.

stem: What does the CMDB Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) provide?

options.text: A centralized framework for identifying and reconciling data from different data sources to maintain CMDB integrity
A way to schedule CAB meetings
A method to calculate change risk
A self-service catalog for ordering items

rationale: IRE is the gatekeeper for CMDB data quality: a central framework that identifies and reconciles records coming from multiple data sources, keeping the CMDB (and some non-CMDB tables) consistent.

distractor_notes.C: Change risk uses the risk lookup, not IRE.
distractor_notes.D: The service catalog is for requesting items.

stem: Which of the following are components or rules that support the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)?
rationale: IRE is supported by identification rules, reconciliation rules, data source rules, de-duplication tasks, and reclassification tasks. Blackout windows and incident priority lookups belong to Change and Incident Management respectively.

distractor_notes.D: Blackout windows are a Change Management scheduling concept.
distractor_notes.E: Priority lookup rules set incident priority, not CMDB identity.

references.title: Components and process of Identification and Reconciliation

stem: Two different data sources both import a record for the same physical server. What prevents the CMDB from ending up with duplicate CIs?
rationale: Identification is exactly what stops duplicates: the IRE matches incoming payloads against existing CIs (using identification rules) so the same server updates one CI instead of spawning a second.

distractor_notes.B: The conflict calendar handles change scheduling, not CI identity.
distractor_notes.C: Auto-close is an Incident Management behavior.
distractor_notes.D: The wish list saves catalog items for later.

stem: How does CMDB Health represent the quality of the CMDB?

options.text: Health indicators such as duplicate CIs, required CI fields
It counts the number of open incidents per CI
It measures the change success score

rationale: CMDB Health rolls indicators — duplicates, required fields, audits — into scores at the class, health group, and service levels, and offers a framework for standardized CI remediation.

distractor_notes.B: Open incident counts are an Incident Management metric.
distractor_notes.C: Change success score is a Change Management measure.
distractor_notes.D: Catalog request volume is a Request Management metric.

stem: What does the CI Class Manager let you do?

options.text: Centrally view, create, or edit class definitions, IRE class settings
Resolve incidents on behalf of agents

rationale: CI Class Manager is the central console for CMDB class work — class definitions, the IRE settings for those classes, CMDB Health, and some Service Mapping definitions.

stem: What can you do with the CI relationship editor?

options.text: View, create, modify, or delete CI relationships

rationale: The relationship editor is where you manage the connections between CIs — viewing, creating, modifying, or deleting relationships — launched from the CI Relations formatter.

distractor_notes.B: Incident priority comes from impact and urgency.
distractor_notes.C: Change approvals happen in Change Management.

stem: What does the CI Relations formatter on the CI form let you do?

options.text: Examine a CI and its relationships in various views, and launch the relationship editor

rationale: The CI Relations formatter is the relationship lens on the CI form — explore the CI's relationships in different views and jump into the relationship editor from there.

distractor_notes.B: Conflict detection is a Change Management feature.
distractor_notes.C: On-hold reasons are an Incident Management field.
distractor_notes.D: Catalog item configuration is a Service Catalog task.

stem: What is the CMDB Query Builder used for?

options.text: Building complex infrastructure and service queries that span multiple CMDB classes, non-CMDB tables

rationale: The Query Builder lets you visually construct rich queries across multiple classes and tables, traversing the relationships that connect CIs — far beyond what a single list filter can express.

distractor_notes.C: Change risk uses the risk lookup.
distractor_notes.D: Bulk incident resolution is Incident Management.

options.text: A central, modernized workspace to search and explore the CMDB, examine health and recent activities
A queue of catalog requests awaiting approval
A list of problems pending root cause analysis

rationale: CMDB Workspace is the modern home base for CMDB work — searching and exploring CIs, checking health and activity, and reaching the dashboards and tools you need.

distractor_notes.B: A request approval queue is Request/Change Management.
distractor_notes.D: The change schedule is Change Management.

stem: What does Baseline CMDB help you do?

options.text: Understand and control the changes that have been made to your CIs in the CMDB
Order catalog items on behalf of other users

rationale: Baseline CMDB captures a reference point so you can see and control how CIs have changed over time — useful for spotting drift and unexpected modifications.

distractor_notes.B: Ordering on behalf is a Service Catalog capability.
distractor_notes.C: Offering pricing is Service Portfolio Management.
distractor_notes.D: Assessing a problem is Problem Management.
